title: Estimation of ambient PM 2.5 in Iraq and Kuwait from 2001 to 2018 using machine learning and remote sensing.
summary: A four-stage model combines satellite aerosol, meteorology, dust and land-use variables, random-forest visibility prediction and sparse ground PM2.5 monitoring to estimate 1-km daily historical exposure in Iraq/Kuwait for 2001–2018. It reports country means of 37 and 41 μg/m³ and spatial/temporal variation. These are model estimates, not a direct continuous monitor record; PM2.5 calibration is sparse.
ai_technology: Random forest predicts visibility from satellite/reanalysis/dust/land-use predictors; a visibility-to-PM2.5 stage and spatial models generate the exposure surface.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Results report cross-validation R² for visibility and PM2.5 stages, then 1-km historical exposure estimates and regional temporal/spatial patterns.
evidence.unknown: Cross-validation withheld visibility stations; PM2.5 fit used sparse monitors in 2017–18 with 2004–05 validation. Three sites/two periods constrain calibration; modeled concentrations remain estimates.
